name: Python
headline: Natural speech, a few lines of Python.
description: Build with the PyAI Python SDK: stream natural speech, transcribe recordings, and start from a runnable project with copyable code and AI agent setup guides.
summary: Stream Speak and transcribe recordings with Hear through one reusable client.
features: Receive audio as it arrives with speech_stream.
Reuse pooled connections across synthesis and transcription requests.
Leave the Hear language hint unset for automatic detection.
needs: A PyAI key. The starter writes speech.wav; add --transcribe call.wav to transcribe your own recording.
note: The starter measures first received bytes, not speaker playback latency. Feed PCM chunks to your audio sink for live playback.
setup:
python3 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
cp .env.example .env
# Fill in .env, then export its values in this shell:
set -a
. ./.env
set +a
python main.py

name: TypeScript
headline: Bring natural voice to your TypeScript app.
description: Build with the PyAI TypeScript SDK: stream speech, transcribe audio, and download a runnable Node.js starter with copyable code and coding agent setup guides.
summary: Use typed requests and native ReadableStream audio in your Node.js backend.
features: Consume speechStream without collecting the whole response.
Preserve backpressure and cancel the reader when stopping early.
Upload a recording with the same authenticated client.
needs: A PyAI key. The starter writes speech.pcm; run npm start -- call.wav to also transcribe a recording.
note: The starter runs on Node.js. Keep secret keys on your backend; use the browser voice-agent guide for frontend authentication.
setup:
npm install
cp .env.example .env
# Fill in .env, then:
npm start

name: Twilio
headline: Give your phone number a natural voice agent.
description: Connect Twilio Media Streams to PyAI Omni with a runnable Node.js voice agent, signed webhook validation, copyable setup commands, and coding agent guidance.
summary: Bridge a Twilio Media Stream to Omni for the complete speech-to-speech loop.
features: Convert Twilio audio to the Omni stream through OmniAgent.bridge.
Let the bridge handle audio pacing and interruptions.
Validate Twilio signatures before accepting webhooks and sockets.
needs: A PyAI key, a Twilio phone number and auth token, and an HTTPS tunnel or deployed server. Set PUBLIC_ORIGIN to its origin.
note: After starting the server, set your Twilio number’s incoming voice webhook to https://YOUR-HOST/voice (POST). Carrier charges apply when you make a call.
setup:
npm install
cp .env.example .env
# Fill in .env, then:
npm start

name: LiveKit

summary: Add Hear and Speak to an existing LiveKit Agents session.
features: Use pyai.STT() and pyai.TTS() in AgentSession.
Receive audio frames as Speak generates them.
Keep your existing room, LLM, tools, and turn-taking configuration.
needs: Only a PyAI key for the included speech.wav smoke test. A complete room agent also needs LiveKit credentials and your chosen LLM; the linked guide covers that setup.
note: This starter tests the TTS adapter without opening a room. LiveKit continues to own your agent loop; the adapter does not create an Omni session.

summary: Plug PyAI speech services into the transport and LLM pipeline you already use.
features: Use PyAISTTService and PyAITTSService as pipeline processors.
Receive TTSAudioRawFrame output for your audio transport.
Keep your existing LLM, context aggregators, and application logic.
needs: Only a PyAI key for the included text-to-WAV pipeline. A conversational bot additionally needs a Pipecat transport and an LLM; follow the linked integration guide.
note: The downloadable starter is a complete text-to-audio pipeline. It does not open a microphone, room, or phone call.
